cards.front: What appears on your credential when you choose to be an organ donor?
cards.back: Choosing to be an organ donor puts a small heart on the front of your credential.

cards.front: Under Indiana's Donor Choice Law, can family members override an adult's choice to donate?
cards.back: Under Indiana's Donor Choice Law, a person aged eighteen or older can declare the wish to be an organ donor, and family members cannot override that choice at death.

cards.front: What does a person under eighteen need to declare the wish to be an organ donor?
cards.back: A person under eighteen can declare the wish to donate only with a parent's or legal guardian's permission, and that adult must consent to donation when the minor dies.

cards.front: How does an adult's donor declaration differ from a minor's?
cards.back: An adult's donor declaration cannot be overridden by family, while a minor's declaration depends on a parent or guardian consenting at the time of death.

cards.front: How can an active-duty service member add an active-duty indicator?
cards.back: An active-duty member of the US Armed Forces can add an active-duty indicator by showing a current Common Access Card (CAC) at a branch during a new issuance or renewal.

cards.front: What document lets a veteran add a veteran indicator?
cards.back: A veteran who was not dishonorably discharged can add a veteran indicator by providing a Department of Defense DD two hundred fourteen that verifies the discharge.

cards.front: What must a surviving spouse of a deceased veteran present for a veteran spouse indicator?
cards.back: A surviving spouse of a deceased veteran can add a veteran spouse indicator by presenting proof of the veteran's discharge or separation, the marriage certificate and the veteran's death certificate.

cards.front: Which document backs each military indicator?
cards.back: An active-duty indicator is backed by a current Common Access Card, a veteran indicator by a DD two hundred fourteen, and a veteran spouse indicator by discharge proof plus marriage and death certificates.

decks.domain: Credential indicators, watercraft, parking placards, and renewing, amending or replacing a credential

cards.front: When must a boat operator carry a valid driver's license?
cards.back: Anyone operating a watercraft whose engine produces more than ten horsepower must carry a valid driver's license.

cards.front: How can a person fifteen or older without a driver's license operate a boat over ten horsepower?
cards.back: A person aged fifteen or older without a driver's license may operate such a watercraft only after finishing a boater education course that the Indiana Department of Natural Resources has approved, and must carry a valid Indiana ID card while doing so.

cards.front: Who may never operate a watercraft with an engine over ten horsepower?
cards.back: Nobody younger than fifteen may operate a watercraft with an engine of more than ten horsepower.

cards.front: How do the boating rules differ for people fifteen or older and those under fifteen?
cards.back: Unlicensed operators aged fifteen or older may run a watercraft exceeding ten horsepower only after completing an approved boater education course and while carrying a valid Indiana identification card, whereas anyone under fifteen is barred from operating one.

cards.front: How can a suspended license or bad boating affect you?
cards.back: A person whose driver's license is suspended may not operate a watercraft, and reckless or intoxicated boating or breaking watercraft laws can add points to the driver record.

cards.front: Who needs an Indiana driver's license when operating a watercraft on boundary waters?
cards.back: On Indiana boundary waters, Indiana residents operating a watercraft must carry an Indiana driver's license, while residents of other states need one only on an embayment, river or stream in Indiana.

cards.front: How do the boundary waters rules differ for Indiana residents and out-of-state residents?
cards.back: Indiana residents on boundary waters must carry an Indiana license, while out-of-state residents need one only on an Indiana embayment, river or stream.

decks.domain: Credential indicators, watercraft, parking placards, and renewing, amending or replacing a credential

cards.front: Who is eligible for a disability parking placard?
cards.back: A disability parking placard is available to people with a permanent or temporary disability, to people issued or eligible for a Disabled Hoosier Veteran plate, and to organizations providing transportation or facilities for people with physical disabilities.

cards.front: What kind of company may apply for a disability parking placard?
cards.back: A company empowered by the state or a political subdivision to run transportation or facility programs for people with physical disabilities may apply for a placard.

cards.front: Who completes the placard application form, and where can it go?
cards.back: To apply, a health care provider (for example a physician, chiropractor, podiatrist, physician's assistant, advanced practice registered nurse, optometrist or ophthalmologist) completes State Form forty-two thousand seventy, which can be taken to any branch or mailed.

cards.front: Who does not need a health care provider's certification for a placard?
cards.back: No health care provider certification is needed for a person who has received or is eligible for a Disabled Hoosier Veteran plate.

cards.front: What does a permanent placard cost, and when does it expire?
cards.back: A permanent placard is free and does not expire unless a provider certifies the disability is no longer permanent or the Indiana Department of Veteran Affairs certifies the holder is no longer a Disabled Hoosier Veteran.

cards.front: How much does a temporary placard cost, and when does it expire?
cards.back: A temporary placard carries a fee and expires on the provider's stated date or one year after issue, whichever comes first.

cards.front: How does a permanent placard differ from a temporary placard?
cards.back: A permanent placard is free and open-ended, while a temporary placard has a fee and lasts at most one year.

cards.front: When does a placard issued to an organization expire?
cards.back: A placard issued to an organization expires on January one of the fourth year after the issue year, or earlier if it stops running programs or facilities for people with disabilities.

cards.front: What can happen if you use an expired placard, and where can you never park?
cards.back: Using an expired placard can lead to a fine, and parking in the diagonally striped area beside a reserved space is never allowed, even with a valid placard.

decks.domain: Credential indicators, watercraft, parking placards, and renewing, amending or replacing a credential

cards.front: What may a person get after losing a credential while living outside Indiana for a while?
cards.back: A person who loses a credential while temporarily living outside Indiana may be able to get an interim credential.

cards.front: Who may renew or replace a credential online, and how often may online renewal be used?
cards.back: If your name and residential address have not changed, you may be eligible to renew or replace online at myBMV.com, and online or BMV Connect kiosk renewal is allowed every other renewal.

cards.front: When does a probationary license expire, and when do other credentials expire?
cards.back: A probationary license expires at twenty-one years and thirty days and may be renewed online if the holder qualifies, while all other credentials expire at midnight on the holder's birthday.

cards.front: How does a probationary license's expiry differ from other credentials?
cards.back: A probationary license ends at twenty-one years and thirty days, whereas every other credential runs out at midnight on the holder's birthday.

cards.front: When does a credential expire if your birthday falls on a day branches are closed?
cards.back: If your birthday falls on a day when branches are closed, the credential expires at midnight on the next business day.

cards.front: Do expiration dates follow the usual rules for residents with temporary lawful status?
cards.back: Credential expiration dates differ for residents with temporary lawful status.

cards.front: What applies to everyone who renews a credential after it expires?
cards.back: Everyone who renews a credential after its expiration date is subject to an administrative penalty.

cards.front: What does renewing a license expired one hundred eighty days to five years require?
cards.back: Renewing a license expired for at least one hundred eighty days but not more than five years requires the administrative penalty, a knowledge exam and a standard vision screening.

cards.front: What does renewing a license expired five years or more require?
cards.back: Renewing a license expired for five years or more requires the administrative penalty plus a knowledge exam, a driving skills exam and a standard vision screening.

cards.front: How do the late-renewal requirements differ by how long a license has been expired?
cards.back: Renewing a driver's license expired from one hundred eighty days up to five years requires an administrative penalty, a knowledge exam, and a standard vision screening, while one expired five years or longer also requires a driving skills exam.

cards.front: How early can a citizen renew a license compared with a lawful temporary resident?
cards.back: US citizens and permanent lawful residents can renew a license or ID card up to twenty-four months before it expires, while people with lawful temporary status can renew only up to thirty days ahead.

cards.front: How early can a learner's permit be renewed?
cards.back: A learner's permit can be renewed up to thirty days before it expires.

cards.front: Which credentials can be renewed twenty-four months early, and which only thirty days early?
cards.back: A citizen or permanent resident may renew a license or ID card as early as twenty-four months ahead, but a learner's permit or a lawful temporary resident's credential only thirty days ahead.

cards.front: Who must pass the knowledge exam to renew a license because of points?
cards.back: A driver aged twenty-one or older with six or more active points must pass the knowledge exam to renew the license.

cards.front: What triggers the knowledge exam at renewal for drivers twenty-one or older?
cards.back: The knowledge exam at renewal is triggered by six or more active points for drivers aged twenty-one or older.

cards.front: How long does a license stay valid after a service member's discharge or return?
cards.back: A license held by someone serving outside Indiana with the US Armed Forces stays valid for ninety days after discharge, post-deployment or the end of the out-of-state service residence.

cards.front: How does a veteran renew an expired license after discharge?
cards.back: To renew an expired license after discharge, a veteran visits a branch with Department of Defense proof of discharge or the long form DD two hundred fourteen, and can add the veteran indicator at that visit.

cards.front: Where does the manual send chauffeur license holders for renewal details?
cards.back: For chauffeur and public passenger chauffeur licenses, the manual sends readers to the For-Hire Endorsement section of Chapter two for renewal, amendment and replacement details.

cards.front: What must you do after legally changing your personal information?
cards.back: After legally changing personal information you must amend your credential, which can be done at any BMV branch.

cards.front: How long do you have to report a change of principal address, and how?
cards.back: A change of principal (legal) address must be reported and an amended credential applied for within thirty days, in person at a branch with Appendix A documents.

cards.front: Where can you change your mailing address?
cards.back: A mailing address can be changed online at myBMV.com, at a BMV Connect kiosk or at a branch.

cards.front: How does changing a principal address differ from changing a mailing address?
cards.back: A principal address change needs a branch visit with documents within thirty days, while a mailing address change can be done online, at a kiosk or at a branch.

cards.front: What are the steps to amend your credential after a name change?
cards.back: For a name change, update Social Security records first, wait at least one business day, then visit a branch within thirty days of the change with Appendix A documents to amend the credential.

cards.front: What does the manual say about replacing an SSA card when your Indiana credential is unexpired?
cards.back: If your Indiana license, permit or ID card is not expired, the manual says the SSA card replacement can be done online at no cost.

cards.front: When can a lost or stolen credential be replaced online, and how many times?
cards.back: A lost or stolen credential can be replaced through myBMV.com or a BMV Connect kiosk when the name and residential address are unchanged, up to ten online replacements before a branch visit is required.

cards.front: What happens after you have replaced a credential online ten times?
cards.back: Online replacement is capped at ten times, after which the holder must replace the credential at a BMV branch.

cards.front: What must you do if anything other than your mailing address has changed and you need a replacement?
cards.back: If anything other than the mailing address has changed, a replacement cannot be ordered online; the holder must amend the credential at a branch within thirty days with Appendix A documents.

recap_hooks.text: A heart on your card means donor; adults decide for themselves, minors need a parent or guardian.
Military indicators need a Common Access Card, a discharge record, or a spouse's discharge, marriage and death papers.
Boats over ten horsepower need a driver's license, or a boater course and ID card from age fifteen.
No one under fifteen may run such a boat, and a suspended driver may not boat at all.
Permanent placards are free and do not expire; temporary placards have a fee and last at most a year.
Never park in the striped aisle, even with a valid placard.
Most credentials expire at midnight on your birthday, and renewing late always brings a penalty.
Expired five years or more means a driving skills exam on top of the knowledge exam and vision screening.
Report a new principal address or a name change within thirty days at a branch.
Mailing address changes and unchanged-detail replacements can be done online.
